propositions: Recovery preflight refuses contexts over 100k chars (c9f7: 121,147 chars) by applying a flat per-context bound that has been manually raised twice and now requires replacement with model-window-derived bounds.
The flat _MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS bound conflates two independent ceilings: physical (single evidence run context window) and economic (recovery fan-out multiplier: context_chars × criteria_count).

A context that fits the model window and stays under the product ceiling (121,147 × 22 = 2.67M < 3.2M worst case) is wrongly refused because the per-axis split is arbitrary rather than deriving from actual capacity.

The physical ceiling must derive from the resolved verifier model's own context window via MODEL_LADDER, not a static constant; the economic ceiling must be explicitly bounded at _MAX_RECOVERY_INPUT_CHARS = 3,200,000 (the ratified worst case: 32 criteria × 100k chars).
d59e's pinned invariants (no elision, full context byte-identical to model, criteria budget ≤ context budget) must remain preserved after refactoring the bounds.
Live Bedrock evidence run confirmed a 115k-char context (exceeding the old 100k bound) completes recovery to a verdict in one request under the window-derived ceiling.
